references.text: Agag is mentioned as the king of the Amalekites whom Saul captured, which connects to the prophecy that Israel's king shall be higher than Agag.
The image of a tree planted by flowing water that bears fruit resembles the metaphor of water flowing from the buckets and offspring at many waters.
The Lord promises to pour out water on the thirsty and streams on the dry ground, and their offspring shall grow up like willows beside flowing brooks.
The image of a tree planted by abundant water that shoots forth branches and bears fruit recalls the prophecy of Israel's growth by many waters.
David's kingdom was exalted, fulfilling the prophecy that Israel's kingdom would be exalted.
David's kingdom became increasingly exalted for the sake of the people of Israel, a fulfillment of Balaam's prophecy.
The psalm describes God's promises to David of an exalted kingdom and that his hand shall be over the sea and the rivers.
